thread:
Maya (PM): heads up — competitor X shipped a 'lite-routing' feature that maps tenant routing policies to model variants. got a seat in sales today where ACME wants parity. thinking we need to decide: quick parity shim or invest in our own differentiated lane? :thinking:

Sam (Eng): saw that. their offer is basically a router + model alias. low-tech. we can sketch a shim in 2 sprints but long-term cost/ops pain.

Jordan (Data): customer telemetry: 3 pilot accounts asked for per-tenant route rules last quarter. ACME is the most vocal. volume isn't huge but it's high value. embedding-heavy workloads would expose cost.

Li (Design): parity vs differentiation tradeoff: parity gives short-term ARR lift; differentiation could be proxying insights + per-tenant quality controls. design impact significant.

Alex (Sales): ACME told me "we'll sign if we can isolate routing per tenant + SLA". They want details by EOW. :grimacing:

Maya (PM): proposal: run a 1-week spike to evaluate two tracks concurrently: A) parity shim (adapter + config UI) — target: ship fast, clear docs + migration guide; B) differentiated lane (per-tenant quality tiers + fallback routing + cost caps) — target: prototype only. deliverables and acceptance criteria listed below.

Sam (Eng): ok. for spike I'll need estimated infra delta. quick shim: add routing table + model alias layer. prototype lane: requires policy engine + telemetry hooks.

Jordan (Data): spike success metrics: perf impact <10% p95 latency, cost delta per request <15%, and we can simulate ACME workload. if not, call it.

Li (Design): acceptance: parity UI flow for admin to set rules end-to-end. prototype screens for tiered quality.

Maya (PM): launch criteria for parity ship (if we go that route):
- docs + migration guide
- UI + API parity with examples
- perf validated on staging
- rollback knob and canary by tenant

Maya (PM): immediate asks: Sam + Jordan go deep on infra perf/cost estimates (2d). Li mock up basic admin flow (3d). Alex collect written ACME requirements (EOD). I'll book a 30m sync Friday to decide.

Sam (Eng): putting notes in this thread: 
```
spike tasks:
- simulate routing rules (in nginx proxy?)
- stub model aliasing layer
- run 10k qps sim with ACME-like sequences
```

pm-bot: Reminder: Maya scheduled Decision Sync on Fri 10:00am

Alex (Sales): looping @Maya (PM) and @Sam (Eng) — ACME willing to pilot canary in prod for 4 weeks, needs rollback guarantee.

Jordan (Data): I'll draft workload generator and baseline numbers by Thurs.

Maya (PM): thanks. if parity is chosen we'll fast-follow with Optimize suggestions to reduce unit cost. If we choose differentiated path, we'll scope a separate RFC. :rocket:

Li (Design): quick thought — if we ship parity, add a tiny telemetry opt-in to gather metrics for the differentiator later.

Sam (Eng): agree. opt-in flag + event schema is low lift.

Maya (PM): perfect. next steps = spike + Friday decision. :thumbsup:
